name: redis_get
description: Get the value of a string key. Returns NULL if the key does not exist.

name: redis_set
description: Set the value of a string key.

name: redis_mget
description: Get multiple values in one round-trip. Keys are passed as a comma-separated string; values come back comma-separated in the same order, with an empty entry for each missing key so positions line up.

name: redis_hget
description: Get the value of a hash field. Returns NULL if the key or field does not exist.

name: redis_hset
description: Set the value of a hash field. Returns the number of fields added as a BIGINT: 1 for a new field, 0 when an existing field is overwritten.

name: redis_hgetall
description: List all (field, value) pairs of a hash as a table.

name: redis_hscan
description: Cursor-paginated scan of a hash's fields. Returns 'next_cursor:field1=value1,...'; re-pass the cursor until it comes back as '0'.

name: redis_hscan_over_scan
description: For every key matching a SCAN pattern, run HSCAN and emit (key, field, value) rows, following both cursors to the end. Matching keys that are not hashes are skipped. The high-throughput discovery primitive for migration / analysis.

name: redis_lpush
description: Push a value onto the head of a list. Returns the length of the list after the push as a BIGINT.

name: redis_lrange
description: Get a range from a list as a comma-separated string.

name: redis_lrange_table
description: Get a range from a list as a table — one row per element. Easier to work with in SQL than the comma-separated form.

name: redis_del
description: Delete a key. Returns TRUE if the key existed and was removed.

name: redis_type
description: Get the Redis type of a key (string / list / hash / set / zset / stream / none).

name: redis_scan
description: Cursor-paginated SCAN of the keyspace, one page per call. Returns 'next_cursor:keys_csv'. Iterate by re-passing the returned cursor until it comes back as '0'.

name: redis_keys
description: List all keys matching a pattern as a table, one row per key. Built on SCAN, not KEYS: it follows the cursor page by page until the keyspace is exhausted, so it doesn't block the server — but it always walks the whole keyspace. Use redis_scan to page manually.

name: redis_expire
description: Set a key's time-to-live in seconds. Returns TRUE if the TTL was set, FALSE if the key does not exist.

name: redis_expireat
description: Expire a key at an absolute Unix timestamp (seconds). Returns TRUE if the expiry was set, FALSE if the key does not exist.

name: redis_ttl
description: Remaining time-to-live in seconds. Returns -1 if the key has no expiry and -2 if the key does not exist.
